transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. What brings you in to see me today?

I guess… the main thing is my eating’s been kind of off lately. I mean, I’m still getting through work and everything, but some days before a shift I’ll realize I’ve only had coffee and maybe a granola bar. And my scrubs are starting to hang a little loose, even though I’m not trying to lose weight. It just seemed like maybe I should get it checked out.
Have you been trying to lose weight?

No, no—I’m not trying to lose weight. If anything, I feel a little awkward that it’s happening. I’ve just been kind of not eating much some days, like coffee and maybe a granola bar before work, and then I notice my scrubs are looser. I’m not doing it on purpose.
Do you ever worry about gaining weight?

Not really, no. I mean, I don’t want to gain a bunch of weight or anything, but I’m not avoiding food because of that. It’s more like my appetite’s just… off. Some days before a shift I’ll only manage coffee and maybe a granola bar, and then I notice my scrubs are looser. I’m not trying for that.
Do you ever eat a lot of food in a short amount of time?

No, not really. It’s more the opposite, I guess. I’m not having these times where I eat a lot all at once. It’s just that some days my eating kind of slips, like I’ll get to a shift and realize I’ve only had coffee and maybe a granola bar. And then I notice my scrubs are looser, which… I know isn’t great.
Do you feel anxious about the possibility of gaining weight?

No, I don’t think I’m anxious about gaining weight. I mean, I guess nobody wants to suddenly gain a lot, but that’s not what’s going on for me. It’s more that my eating’s been kind of off… like some days before a shift I barely get down coffee and a granola bar, and then I notice my scrubs hanging looser. I’m not trying to lose weight, if that makes sense.
Do you have any fear about gaining weight?

No, I wouldn’t say I’m afraid of gaining weight. I know I probably sound like I’m focused on it, but it’s really more that my eating has been off. Some days before work I barely get down coffee and maybe a granola bar, and then I notice my scrubs are hanging kind of loose. I’m not trying to lose weight or anything.
How much weight have you lost?

I’m not totally sure of the exact number… I haven’t been tracking it closely. I just know my scrubs have been fitting looser, and I’ve had days where I barely get coffee and a granola bar down before a shift. It’s not intentional or anything.
Do you find yourself not wanting to eat because you're just not interested in food?

Yeah… I think that’s closer to it. It’s not like I’m avoiding food on purpose, I just don’t feel that interested sometimes. Before a shift I’ll tell myself I’ll eat something, and then it ends up being just coffee and maybe a granola bar. I know that’s probably not great. And then I notice my scrubs are looser, which is what kind of made me bring it up.
Have you noticed a decrease in enjoyment of activities you normally like to do?

Yeah… I mean, maybe a little more than I’d like to admit. I used to run in Van Cortlandt Park, take photos, play chess with friends—normal stuff I actually liked. Lately I’ll think about doing it and then I kind of tell myself, “What’s the point?” and I end up just sitting at home scrolling on my phone or checking my budget spreadsheet. It sounds kind of pathetic when I say it out loud, but… yeah, I’ve noticed it.
Would you say you've lost a significant amount of weight over the past few months?

Yeah… I think so. I don’t know the exact number, so I don’t want to overstate it, but my scrubs have definitely been hanging looser. And it’s not like I’m trying to lose weight—it’s more that my eating’s been really off. Some days before a shift I barely get down coffee and a granola bar.
Have you been feeling sad or depressed most of the time?

Yeah… I guess I have. I don’t want to make it sound dramatic, but most mornings I wake up with this heavy, kind of hollow feeling, like the day’s already ruined before I even put on my badge. I still get up and do what I’m supposed to do, but… it’s there a lot. Does that make sense?
Do you find pleasure in things you're doing nowadays?

Not really, no. I mean… I don’t want to make it sound worse than it is, but the things I used to enjoy—running in Van Cortlandt Park, taking photos, playing chess with friends—I just don’t get much out of them lately. I’ll think about doing one of them and then it’s like, “What’s the point?” So I end up just sitting at home, scrolling on my phone or checking my budget spreadsheet. I know that’s probably not the healthiest answer.
Do you feel like you've been moving more slowly than usual?

Sometimes, yeah. I mean… not all the time. At work it can go either way, which probably sounds weird. There are times I’m sort of pacing around the supply area, checking the same drawers more than I need to. And then other times I’m just… slow. Like drawing up labels or answering a patient takes me twice as long as it should. I try to cover it, but I’ve noticed it.
Have you lost more than 5% of your body weight over the past month?

I’m not totally sure on the exact percentage… I haven’t been, like, tracking it carefully. But yeah, my appetite’s been pretty off. Some days before a shift I barely manage coffee and maybe a granola bar, and then I just kind of keep going.

And my scrubs have been fitting looser lately, hanging on me more than they used to. I’m not trying to lose weight or anything. I don’t know if that counts as more than 5%, but… it’s noticeable.
Have you lost more than 5% of your body weight over the past month?

I don’t know the exact number, honestly. I haven’t weighed myself enough to say it’s definitely more than 5%. But… my eating’s been off enough that some days I’m only getting down coffee and maybe a granola bar before work, and then I just push through the shift.

My scrubs have been hanging looser, too, and I’m not trying to lose weight. So… yeah, it’s noticeable, but I don’t want to overstate it if that makes sense.
Have you noticed a significant change in how your clothes fit over the past month?

Yeah… I guess I have. My scrubs have been fitting looser, kind of hanging on me more than they used to. I don’t want to make it sound dramatic, but I’m not trying to lose weight or anything.

My eating’s just been off — some days before a shift I barely get down coffee and maybe a granola bar, and then I just keep going. So… yes, I’ve noticed it.
Have you been having any thoughts about harming yourself?

Um… not like a plan or anything. I don’t want you to think I’m, you know, about to do something.

But… yeah, I have had thoughts like… it might be easier if I just didn’t wake up. Or if I could just kind of disappear for a while. I haven’t made a plan to hurt myself, though.
How long have you been feeling this heavy, hollow feeling most mornings?

It’s been… longer than I’d like to admit. The really steady heaviness, like most mornings waking up with that hollow feeling, probably settled in maybe a year and a few months ago.

I’d say around a year and four months, give or take. I kept thinking it would pass or I’d snap out of it, so I didn’t really mark the date or anything.
Are there any activities that you still enjoy doing?

I mean… a little, maybe. I don’t want to say I enjoy nothing, because that sounds… I don’t know, worse than I mean.

I used to run in Van Cortlandt Park, take photos, play chess with friends — stuff like that. Lately I mostly talk myself out of it, like there’s no point, and then I end up just sitting at home scrolling on my phone or checking my budget spreadsheet. It’s not great, but… yeah, that’s kind of where I’m at.
How long have you been feeling like you don't enjoy the things you used to do?

Probably about the same stretch as the heaviness… maybe a year and four months or so.

It wasn’t like everything stopped overnight. I just gradually stopped wanting to do the things I used to like, and then it kind of became normal. I know that’s probably not great, but… yeah, roughly that long.
